**Step 1 — Scene:** A vegetable salad with leafy greens, grilled aubergine (eggplant), and asparagus, with a visible oily sheen.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A square dinner plate, approximately 26–28 cm across. Using a 26 cm circular approximation gives an area of **3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Mixed leafy greens (mainly rocket/arugula), grilled aubergine, asparagus, and oil-based dressing. A few reddish leaves appear to belong to the salad mix.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate area covered | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed leafy greens | 34% | 180 cm² × 2.5 cm = 450 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 68 g | 25 | 17 kcal |
| Grilled aubergine | 17% | 90 cm² × 1.8 cm = 162 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 97 g | 35 | 34 kcal |
| Asparagus | 12% | 64 cm² × 1.8 cm = 115 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 75 g | 22 | 17 kcal |
| Oil-based dressing | Thin coating, overlapping vegetables | Approximately 8 ml | 0.92 g/ml | 7 g | 884 | 62 kcal |

The food footprints total **63%** of the plate. Dressing coats those same areas rather than covering an additional region. Oil is counted separately, so the vegetable energy values exclude added oil.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **247 g and 130 kcal** is plausible for this moderately piled vegetable salad. The dressing amount is the main energy uncertainty; no substantial protein or starch is clearly visible.
